_README: FROZEN ODE-ORACLE GOLDENS. Every `ode_value` here was MEASURED by running the live ODE arm (OMNISIM_FORCE_ODE=1) of the Newton parity suite on the machine named in `provenance`, on the date recorded on each measurement. src/ode is being deleted; the ODE arm will no longer exist, so these numbers are the parity evidence the migration was built on and the only remaining reference the tests can compare against. NEVER hand-edit a value here, and never add one that was not measured. If a Newton change makes a test fail against a golden, that is the signal the golden exists to produce -- investigate the change, do not retune the number. `newton_value_at_freeze` records what the Newton arm read in the SAME session, so a later drift can be attributed. `asserted_against_golden: false` marks a measurement kept as historical record only, because the two backends legitimately disagree there (documented per entry).

weld.oracle_status_note: IMPORTANT -- the ODE arm here was NEVER a numerical oracle. Both arms were judged independently against the SAME absolute semantic thresholds (hold_drift < 1e-3; payload airborne z >= 1.0; released payload z <= 0.6; rupture sag >= 0.05 or on the floor); no assertion ever compared an ODE number to a Newton number. So the thresholds are what the rewritten Newton-only test keeps, and the ODE numbers below are frozen as HISTORICAL RECORD (asserted_against_golden: false). The rupture path in particular diverges BY DESIGN and the divergence is measured here: ODE RATCHETS (autoLock re-captures the payload each tick, so it creeps 1.2868 -> 1.2079, sag 0.0789 m) while Newton's softer engage transient lets the payload escape recapture and reach the floor (sag 1.1775 m). Both are 'the rupture fired'; freezing ODE's 0.0789 as an equality target would be wrong.

kinematic_native.oracle_status_note: The push MAGNITUDE was never an equality target: the pre-freeze test asserted the displacement bar HARD on the Newton arm and only WARNED on an ODE shortfall, because ODE resolves the per-tick 0.02 m penetration through ERP and MuJoCo through its contact solver. Measured divergence: ODE pushed the ball 1.1295 m, Newton 1.8982 m -- both far above the 0.15 m bar. Frozen as record only. The REST height, by contrast, is a genuine parity number (ODE 0.6496076 vs Newton 0.6496328, 2.5e-5 apart) and IS asserted against the golden.

smoke_lane.what_it_pinned_before: A single blanket env['OMNISIM_FORCE_ODE'] = '1' applied to EVERY smoke world (run_smoke.py, formerly ~line 329). Rationale in the code comment: the smoke worlds are legacy deterministic-regression tests with ODE-tuned golden values, and contact_points is built on ODE-specific ContactProperties (softCFM/softERP).
smoke_lane.what_changed: The blanket pin is GONE. The lane now runs test_suite.py once per backend group: everything not flagged runs on the engine default (Newton/MuJoCo, sidecar-confirmed), and a short per-world `requires_ode` list -- each carrying its own measured `ode_reason` -- runs under the process-level force. Verdict outcomes are unchanged (all four active worlds still PASS); what changed is that the three real ODE dependencies are now individually named and attributed instead of hidden behind one env var.

empty-world-startup.default_backend_verdict: PASS (startup only; not under tests/<group>/worlds/, so it owes no OK: verdict)

api-accelerometer.default_backend_verdict: FAIL -- 'The Accelerometer doesn't return the right acceleration.'
api-accelerometer.root_cause: NUE world. OmNewtonBackend hardcodes newton.ModelBuilder(up_axis=newton.Axis.Z) and never reads WorldInfo.coordinateSystem, so set_gravity() projects WorldInfo.gravity onto the WRONG up axis. The test asserts gravity reads +9.8 on Y.
api-accelerometer.corroborating_measurement: Minimal probe, same session: a 1 kg ball in an ENU world falls from z=3 and rests at z=0.099 (correct). The same ball in an NUE world spawned at y=3 NEVER falls in y (y=3.000 at step 15360) and instead drifts to z=+384 m off the implicit z=0 plane. Newton sidecar confirms Newton drove both.
api-accelerometer.world_level_pin_insufficient: WorldInfo.defaultPhysicsBackend "ode" does NOT restore this verdict (measured). It only redirects Solids still on "auto"; OMNISIM_FORCE_ODE additionally makes odeForced() true, which stops the engine building a Newton world at all (OmSimulationWorld.cpp:226). The two levers are not equivalent -- an open gap.

physics-contact-points.default_backend_verdict: FAIL -- 'Cone is not rotated as much as expected.' (the -rotation[3] > 2.44 assertion)
physics-contact-points.root_cause: Genuinely ODE-contact-semantics dependent: the world declares ODE-path WorldInfo.contactProperties (softCFM 1e-05, softERP 0.0138, bounce, coulombFriction) which the Newton backend ignores, so the mesh cone settles on the ramp differently.

protos-template-deterministic.default_backend_verdict: FAIL -- 'Non-deterministic procedural PROTO nodes should have different sizes (0.000000 = 0.000000)'
protos-template-deterministic.root_cause: NUE world, same hardcoded-Z-up root cause as api-accelerometer, different symptom: Newton's implicit ground plane is added at z=0 in the RAW authored frame, which in an NUE world is a VERTICAL wall through the origin -- exactly where this world's four DistanceSensors sit and exactly along the axis they fire. All four read 0.000000. The test is about procedural PROTO seeding, not physics; it is collateral damage.

rendering-normals.status: skipped in the manifest for a pre-existing WREN offscreen-camera reason, unrelated to physics

smoke_lane.blocking_finding: ODE DELETION BLOCKER, not a test problem: the Newton backend does not honour WorldInfo.coordinateSystem at all -- newton.ModelBuilder(up_axis=newton.Axis.Z) is hardcoded in OmNewtonBackend.cpp, gravity is projected onto that axis by set_gravity(), and the implicit ground plane is placed at raw z=0. Any non-ENU world (NUE, and by inspection any other coordinateSystem) therefore gets zero effective gravity along its real up axis plus a stray plane cutting through the scene. Two of the four active smoke worlds are NUE. This will silently break every non-ENU world in the tree the moment ODE stops being the fallback.
